about: Published experiments for levtrap to reproduce (C3, issue #15). Every number in a verified entry was read from the paper (arXiv full text), with its location; wanted entries were read too but lack parameters a Setup needs (see 'missing'). references.md is the readable version, with the values the wanted papers do state.

verified.id: short slug, also the preset name
verified.slot: one of: single_beam_tweezer | counter_propagating_or_standing_wave | linear_paul | ring_paul | hybrid_paul_optical | parabolic_mirror | dark_trap
verified.setup: a Setup file (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 4); must pass levtrap.setup.parse unless schema_gaps is non-empty (SI units: environment.pressure in Pa, not mbar)
verified.schema_gaps: list of setup keys that the current schema does not support yet, written as ARCHITECTURE.md section 4 says the future schema will (e.g. focus.kind = 'parabolic_mirror')
verified.provenance: map from setup key path to {value, source, flag}; flag is 'stated' (printed in the paper), 'inferred' (worked out from printed values, working in source) or 'assumed' (not in the paper; the value levtrap needs, and why it does not matter for the expected quantities); source names page/section/figure/table
verified.expected: list of {quantity, value, unit, source, tolerance_rel, why}; quantity is a name levtrap.validation.quantity reads (frequency.x|y|z|max|min, depth.kT|K, gas_damping, secular.exact|pseudopotential.<axis>, recoil_heating.<axis>, reheating.<axis>, or a ratio of two of them, e.g. frequency.y/frequency.x, with unit '1')
verified.known_disagreement: optional {issue: N}: the entry disagrees with levtrap beyond its tolerance and issue #N tracks it; tests/test_literature.py marks it xfail. Never widen the tolerance instead (C4, issue #16)
verified.agreement_note: what agreement to expect and why

wanted.citation: as above; metadata_source says where the bibliographic data came from
wanted.skeleton: field kinds and geometry only (no numbers), as they would appear in the Setup
wanted.schema_support: 'current' if the current Setup schema can express the trap, else 'future' with schema_gaps
wanted.needed: parameters to read from the paper
wanted.expected_quantities: measured quantities to read from the paper
wanted.agreement_note: what agreement to expect once the numbers are in, and why
wanted.read: after C3: what the paper does state, in words (no numbers here; references.md has them with locations)
wanted.missing: after C3: the parameters the paper does not state, without which levtrap cannot be compared with it

citation.authors: V. Jain, J. Gieseler, C. Moritz, C. Dellago, R. Quidant, L. Novotny
citation.title: Direct Measurement of Photon Recoil from a Levitated Nanoparticle
citation.metadata_source: title and authors checked against the arXiv PDF (v2); journal and DOI from the publisher listing (not printed on the preprint)

trap.fields[0].power.source: arXiv:1603.03420v2 p. 2: 'power P0 = 70 mW'; Fig. 3, 4 captions: 'focal power P0 = 70 mW'. Where it was measured is not stated

trap.fields[0].focus.NA.source: arXiv:1603.03420v2 p. 2: 'objective of numerical aperture NA = 0.9'. Filling factor / effective NA not stated

trap.fields[0].polarisation.source: arXiv:1603.03420v2 p. 2: 'x axis defines the direction of polarization'

trap.fields[0].mode.source: not stated; a Gaussian beam is assumed (the paper's own theory uses a Gaussian focus, p. 3)

particle.k.source: not stated; silica is taken as lossless at 1064 nm

particle.density.source: arXiv:1603.03420v2 p. 3: 'ρSiO2 = 2200 kg/m3' (mass 1.14e-18 kg at R = 49.8 nm, levtrap 1.138e-18)

environment.temperature.source: not stated; room temperature assumed. Enters only the gas damping, which is not compared

environment.gas.source: not stated. Enters only the gas damping and heating, which this entry does not compare (jain2016_recoil_r527 does)

environment.medium_index.source: vacuum: arXiv:1603.03420v2 pressures of 1e-8 mbar and below

particle.radius.source: arXiv:1603.03420v2 Fig. 2 caption and p. 3: 'R = 49.8 nm'. Uncertainty and method not stated

environment.pressure.source: arXiv:1603.03420v2 Fig. 2 caption: lowest of '6.6e-4, 1.1e-5 and 2e-8 mbar'; 2e-08 mbar = 2e-06 Pa (the Setup's pressure is in Pa; C3 first entered the mbar value as Pa, #61)

expected.source: arXiv:1603.03420v2 p. 2: 'oscillation frequencies for the x and z axes are 123 kHz and 49 kHz'
expected.why: effective NA and power at the focus are not stated (agreement_note)
as frequency.x; the axial frequency is the most sensitive to the shape of the focus

expected.source: inferred from arXiv:1603.03420v2 p. 2: 123 kHz / 150 kHz = 0.820. Jain's thesis (ETH 2017, p. 73) gives 129 kHz for x on the same data (0.860)
expected.why: power-free: the ratio tests the shape of the focus alone. ±5 % as for zheng2020_ratios: an ideal objective against a real one; the frequencies are printed to 1 kHz (under 1 %)

expected.source: inferred from arXiv:1603.03420v2 p. 2: 49 kHz / 150 kHz = 0.327

verified.agreement_note: levtrap's lens is an ideal aplanatic focus filled to NA 0.9 with all 70 mW at the focus; the paper states neither the filling factor nor how P0 was measured. Expect the absolute frequencies to within tens of percent; ±20 % is the tolerance. levtrap is 23-57 % stiffer (issue #61). The ratios fx/fy and fz/fy do not depend on the power; with the stated focus levtrap gives 0.719 and 0.367. No filling of an ideal NA 0.9 objective matches both: 0.7 gives 0.824 and 0.356, 0.5 gives 0.883 and 0.332 (#61; the axial is too stiff as for zheng2020_ratios, #70).

trap.fields[0].power.source: arXiv:1603.03420v2 p. 2: 'power P0 = 70 mW'; Fig. 3, 4 captions: 'focal power P0 = 70 mW'. Where it was measured is not stated

trap.fields[0].focus.NA.source: arXiv:1603.03420v2 p. 2: 'objective of numerical aperture NA = 0.9'. Filling factor / effective NA not stated

trap.fields[0].polarisation.source: arXiv:1603.03420v2 p. 2: 'x axis defines the direction of polarization'

trap.fields[0].mode.source: not stated; a Gaussian beam is assumed (the paper's own theory uses a Gaussian focus, p. 3)

particle.k.source: not stated; silica is taken as lossless at 1064 nm

particle.density.source: arXiv:1603.03420v2 p. 3: 'ρSiO2 = 2200 kg/m3' (mass 1.14e-18 kg at R = 49.8 nm, levtrap 1.138e-18)

environment.temperature.source: not stated; room temperature assumed. Enters the gas heating in reheating.y

environment.gas.source: not stated. It matters here: it sets the gas heating in reheating.y (He instead of N2 lowers it 2.6x; the residual gas of an ultrahigh vacuum is mostly H2). levtrap's gas damping agrees with the paper's Eq. 7 for N2 to 2 %

environment.medium_index.source: vacuum: arXiv:1603.03420v2 pressures of 1e-8 mbar and below

environment.pressure.source: arXiv:1603.03420v2 Fig. 4 caption: '3 × 10−8 mbar' (Fig. 4a); 3e-08 mbar = 3e-06 Pa (the Setup's pressure is in Pa; C3 first entered the mbar value as Pa, #61)

expected.source: arXiv:1603.03420v2 p. 4: 'Γ1 = (20.9 ± 0.2) kHz', the reheating rate along y with the feedback off (Eq. 12); the paper takes it as Γrecoil, assuming the gas heating negligible below 1e-7 mbar
expected.why: the paper's own theory differs from its measurements by up to 35 %; radius uncertainty not stated (rate ∝ R³ at fixed power)

verified.agreement_note: What the paper measures is the total reheating (Eq. 12: n(t) ≈ n0 + Γ t with the feedback off): recoil plus gas. At 3e-8 mbar levtrap's gas heating (N2) is 5.7e3 /s, about as large as its recoil (6.2e3 /s at its 210 kHz): the paper's assumption that gas heating is negligible does not hold for this rate. So the entry compares reheating.y. levtrap gives 11.9e3 /s against 20.9e3 measured; the rest follows the focus (the frequencies, #61) and the unstated gas.

trap.fields[0].power.source: arXiv:2002.02320v1 p. 5: 'the 1064 nm Gaussian beam laser (∼ 200 mW)'; where it was measured is not stated. Only frequency ratios are compared, and they do not depend on the power

trap.fields[0].focus.NA.source: arXiv:2002.02320v1 Suppl. p. 7: 'the numerical aperture (NA) of the objective was 0.9' (Nikon CFI LU Plan Fluor EPI 100X)

trap.fields[0].focus.filling.source: arXiv:2002.02320v1 Suppl. p. 7-8: 'a Gaussian intensity distribution with a beam diameter of 4.5 mm which was measured with a CCD camera beam profiler' and 'The back pupil diameter of the objective was 3.6 mm': 4.5 mm / 3.6 mm = 1.25 (the diameter is taken as the 1/e² one, which a Gaussian fit of a beam profiler gives)

trap.fields[0].polarisation.source: arXiv:2002.02320v1 Suppl. p. 7: 'the laser was linearly polarized along X axis'

particle.radius.source: arXiv:2002.02320v1 p. 4 and Table II: 'R = 75.4 ± 1.5 nm' (from the gas damping with the calibrated mass)

particle.density.source: arXiv:2002.02320v1 p. 4: 'the density was ρ = 2.02 ± 0.10 g/cm3'

particle.n.source: not stated; silica at 1064 nm. In the Rayleigh regime (k a = 0.45) the frequency ratios hardly depend on it

particle.k.source: not stated; silica is taken as lossless

environment.gas.source: arXiv:2002.02320v1 Table II: 'mass of the air molecule'

environment.pressure.source: arXiv:2002.02320v1 Fig. 6: the frequency sweeps at 1e-5 mbar = 1e-3 Pa; at which pressure the ratios were taken is not stated. The conservative trap, and so its frequencies, do not depend on it

environment.medium_index.source: vacuum chamber, pressures of mbar and below

expected.source: arXiv:2002.02320v1 Suppl. p. 8: 'the natural frequency ratio between X, Y, and Z should be 1.31 : 1 : 2.93, comparing with the experimental result 1.27 : 1 : 3.07.' The ratios are f_Y/f_i: with f_X = 135450 Hz (Table II), f_Y = 1.27 f_X = 172 kHz, which is where Fig. 6b's Y sweep lies
expected.why: the paper's own model of an ideal NA 0.9 objective filled by the measured beam, the model levtrap shares, misses its measurement by 3 % (1.31 vs 1.27) and 5 % (2.93 vs 3.07); the paper puts this down to an objective designed for visible light and to the beam's shape. levtrap cannot be expected to do better than that model, so ±5 %

verified.agreement_note: Frequency ratios only: the power at the focus is not stated, but the ratios depend on the shape of the focus alone, which the paper pins down (NA, measured beam diameter, pupil diameter). Expect levtrap to land where the paper's own ideal-objective model does (1.31 and 2.93), within the ±5 % by which that model misses the measurement. levtrap gets f_y/f_x = 1.302 (+2.5 %) and f_y/f_z = 2.859 (−6.9 %): the axial frequency is too stiff (issue #70).

citation.journal: J. Phys. B: At. Mol. Opt. Phys. 50, 245501 (2017)
citation.metadata_source: arXiv full text (preprint as posted; the journal version was not available here); web-search index (arXiv listing metadata); not checked against the paper

wanted.trap_type: retro-reflected beam forming an optical lattice (standing wave), silica particle, vacuum (geometry to be confirmed from the text)
needed: power in each pass and the retro-reflection loss
focusing NA or waist of each pass and the relative focus positions
expected_quantities: trap frequencies along x, y, z
linewidths vs pressure (the paper's subject)
wanted.agreement_note: The axial frequency of a standing wave is set by the fringe contrast, i.e. by how well the returning beam overlaps the incoming one; this is seldom stated, so expect the axial frequency to tens of percent and the radial frequencies (set mostly by the waist and power) to be closer. Model as two coherent beams with opposite directions.
wanted.read: A single 1550 nm beam, retro-reflected into a standing wave (one-dimensional lattice); elliptical waists in x and y; silica of nominal radius; trap frequencies along x, y and z; linewidths against pressure.
missing: the beam is elliptical (two waists): the Setup's focus has one NA or waist
power and focus position of the returning pass, and the fringe contrast
the radius of the particle whose frequencies are given (radii vary from particle to particle)
wanted.why_not_verified: the elliptical focus cannot be expressed, and the returning pass is not described
